ocil:questionnaire.ocil:title: Change the Default BAScontrol Admin Password
Maintain BAScontrol22D on a Current Approved Firmware Revision
Use a Static IP Address for Fixed BAScontrol22D Installations
Configure BAScontrol22D Timezone to Map to UTC or GMT

ocil:boolean_question.ocil:question_text: Access the BAScontrol22D web interface and open System Config > Admin. Review the configured administrative account and verify the password has been changed from the vendor-default value to an organization-approved password. If the administrative password is still set to the default value, this is a finding. Is it the case that the BAScontrol22D admin password is still set to the default value?

Access the BAScontrol22D web interface and review the displayed firmware revision. Compare the installed revision to the currently approved firmware baseline for the deployment or the latest vendor-approved revision in local maintenance guidance. If the controller firmware is out of date or not approved for deployment, this is a finding. Is it the case that the controller firmware is not current or not approved for deployment?

Access the BAScontrol22D web interface and open System Config > Admin. In the Enable Protocol section, verify the FTP option is not selected. If FTP is enabled without explicit authorization, this is a finding. Is it the case that FTP is enabled on the controller?

Access the BAScontrol22D web interface and open Set Time. In the NTP Configuration section, verify:
- NTP Enabled is selected - NTP Server is set to an approved time source - Refresh is configured according to site requirements
If NTP is disabled or not configured with an approved time source, this is a finding. Is it the case that NTP is not enabled or is not configured with an approved time server?

Access the BAScontrol22D web interface and open System Config > Wired/IP. Review the IP Mode setting. For fixed installations, verify it is set to STATIC and that the configured address, netmask, and gateway values match the approved network design. If a fixed installation is configured for DHCP, this is a finding. Is it the case that the controller is configured to use DHCP for a fixed installation?

Access the BAScontrol22D web interface and open Set Time. In the NTP Configuration section, review the configured Time Zone value and verify it maps to UTC or GMT as required by the site. If the configured timezone does not map to UTC or GMT, this is a finding. Is it the case that the BAScontrol22D timezone is not configured to map to UTC or GMT?

Access the BAScontrol22D web interface and open System Config > Admin. In the Enable Protocol section, review the configured protocol set, including BACnet/IP, Sedona, BACnet MS/TP, Modbus, Wall Setter, and FTP when present. Verify that only the protocols required for the approved deployment remain enabled. If unnecessary protocols remain enabled, this is a finding. Is it the case that one or more unused BAScontrol22D protocols remain enabled?

Access the BAScontrol22D main interface and verify that the BASbackup function has been used to save a current known-good configuration. Review local administrative records or the designated backup repository and confirm that a recent backup exists for the deployed controller. If a current BASbackup configuration is not available, this is a finding. Is it the case that a current BASbackup configuration is not available?

Using the controller's approved management interface, review its device information and verify that the model is BAScontrol22D and the hardware revision is 4. If the model or hardware revision does not match, this is a finding. Is it the case that the controller cannot be identified as a supported BAScontrol22D4 device?
